title: All-Inclusive in Tučepi 2027: Hotels, Prices, Who It Suits
metaDescription: One true all-inclusive hotel exists in Tučepi: Bluesun Neptun. Prices per person, what is included, versus half-board and apartments, plus nearby options.
content:
## Does Tučepi Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes, but only one. **Bluesun Hotel Neptun** sells a true all-inclusive board and is the only classic all-inclusive hotel in the village itself. It stands on the Slatina beach, on the street Slatina in Tučepi, and is marketed as a family hotel with an outdoor pool, a children's pool and an entertainment programme.

The other large hotels do not follow the same model. Bluesun Hotel Alga sells breakfast and half-board but not a classic all-inclusive. Bluesun Hotel Jadran is a breakfast-oriented property. Some small hotels and villas appear under "all-inclusive" filters on booking sites, but a filter match is not a guarantee. Always check the board type on the confirmation page before paying.

## What Is Included at Bluesun Hotel Neptun

The board covers breakfast, a late continental breakfast, lunch, an afternoon snack and dinner. Drinks with meals in the restaurant include red and white wine, beer and soft drinks such as cola, orange juice, iced tea and tonic. Sunbeds and parasols at the hotel pool are free for guests, and the programme includes children's animation, sports and evening entertainment.

This is "all-inclusive" in the Croatian sense, not the Turkish or Caribbean sense. Drinks are tied mainly to meals and set bars, not unlimited premium spirits around the clock. Cocktails, imported spirits, coffee specialties and excursions are normally extra. Guests who expect a wristband and unlimited top-shelf drinks will be disappointed.

## Price Per Person Per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

These are rough ranges based on current listings for two adults sharing a double room. Exact rates swing by date, room type and booking window.

| Option | Shoulder (May–June, September) | Peak (mid-July to August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Neptun) | €60–90 | €130–190 |
| Half-board (Alga, other hotels) | €55–80 | €110–160 |
| Bed and breakfast | €45–70 | €95–140 |
| Private apartment, room only | €20–30 | €30–50 |

A four-night all-inclusive package at Neptun has been advertised from about €660 per person, or roughly €165 per night, so the peak figure is realistic. Children usually get large discounts or free stays when sharing a room with two adults, and this shifts the maths in favour of hotels for families.

An apartment looks much cheaper on paper. Add food, though, and the gap narrows. In Tučepi, a restaurant dinner with a drink runs about €20–35 per adult, and a supermarket-based day costs about €15–25 per person. A couple self-catering in peak season usually still spends 30–45% less than on all-inclusive.

## Who Should Book All-Inclusive in Tučepi

**Families with children under 10.** Meals at fixed times, a children's pool, animation and no bill at the end are the real benefits. Small children eat early and tire quickly, and a buffet handles this better than a konoba terrace at 21:00.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** Shopping, cooking and cleaning are not worth the effort on a short trip. A hotel with the beach in front removes the logistics.

**Travelers who dislike planning.** Neptun is one block from the main promenade, so the village is still reachable on foot.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

**Stays of a week or more.** Eating the same buffet for seven days gets old fast, and Tučepi has about 30 restaurants and bakeries worth trying. Most travelers overestimate how much they will eat and drink at an all-inclusive buffet. Many people on a beach holiday only use lunch and dinner fully.

**Couples and groups of friends.** Apartments split four ways come to €15–25 per person per night in shoulder season. All-inclusive does not compete on price.

**Anyone planning day trips.** Biokovo, Makarska, Brela and the Pelješac ferry from Drvenik mean you will often eat elsewhere. You pay for meals you skip.

The honest verdict: all-inclusive in Tučepi makes sense for families in July and August, when restaurants fill and prices rise. Outside peak, half-board or an apartment gives better value, and the village's restaurants are good enough that skipping them is a loss.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Options Outside Tučepi

- **Adults only, further south:** TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće is a 4-star all-inclusive, adults-only (16+) beachfront resort. Check the transfer time before booking.
- **Makarska (about 7 km):** several hotels sell half-board, such as Aminess Khalani and Hotel Park, but a classic all-inclusive is rare.
- **Omiš (about 55 km):** Sagitta is an all-inclusive holiday resort with a children's club and buffet meals.

For families, Neptun in Tučepi is the most direct all-inclusive option on this stretch of coast.

## Insider Tips

- Book Neptun early. The best rates appear with early-booking discounts, and promotions of up to 40% off have been run around Black Friday.
- Compare the room-only price on booking sites with the all-inclusive price. The board supplement is often only €25–40 per adult per day.
- Slatina beach is pebble, so water shoes help. The quieter stretches lie toward the old village of Kraj.
- Splitting the stay is a smart compromise. Spend 3–4 nights at Neptun, then move to an apartment for the rest.

## Getting There

Tučepi is about 1 hour 15 minutes from Split by car or bus, roughly 80 km along the coast road. The nearest airport is Split, with Dubrovnik roughly 2.5 hours away.

faq.question: Are there all-inclusive hotels in Tučepi?
faq.answer: Yes, one. Bluesun Hotel Neptun is the only classic all-inclusive hotel in the village, with full board, snacks and drinks with meals. Other hotels such as Bluesun Hotel Alga sell breakfast or half-board.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost in Tučepi per person?
faq.answer: Roughly €60–90 per person per night in shoulder season and €130–190 in July and August. Prices depend on room type, dates and how early you book. Children's discounts can lower the family total considerably.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Tučepi?
faq.answer: No. All-inclusive typically costs about €10–30 per person more per night than half-board. It adds lunch, an afternoon snack and more drinks, which only pays off if you use them.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive worth it for families in Tučepi?
faq.answer: It is worth it for families with children under about 10, especially in peak season. Fixed meal times, a children's pool and animation reduce effort and spending. Families with teenagers who want to explore tend to prefer an apartment.

faq.question: Where is the nearest adults-only all-inclusive to Tučepi?
faq.answer: TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće is a 4-star adults-only (16+) all-inclusive resort. It is a short drive from Tučepi. Confirm transfer times when booking.

faq.question: What is not included in all-inclusive in Tučepi?
faq.answer: Cocktails, premium spirits, specialty coffees, spa treatments and excursions are normally extra. Always check the hotel's list of included drinks and hours before booking.

quickAnswer: Tučepi has one classic all-inclusive hotel: Bluesun Hotel Neptun, on the Slatina beach. It covers breakfast, lunch, an afternoon snack, dinner and house drinks with meals. Expect roughly €60–90 per person per night in shoulder season and €130–190 in peak. Nearby alternatives are in Makarska and Omiš.
